newsitem.title: UK: Australian scientists use lasers to measure coral.
newsitem.headline: Australian scientists use lasers to measure coral.

text.p: Australian scientists reported on Wednesday that they had found a way to use lasers to accurately measure the growth of corals, which they discovered grew mostly at night.
The surprising finding sheds new light on how coral grows and could help to find ways to deal with damage done by pollution, they wrote in a letter to the science journal Nature.

"Our method is non-destructive and allows us to return to the same colony over and over again, in different seasons, after catastrophic events, or at the onset or removal of pollution or other stressors," Razi Vago and colleagues at the Australian Institute of Marine Science in Townsville, Queensland, wrote.
The underwater laser measures small differences in diffraction patterns produced by the laser beam as it is focused on a tip of growing coral.
Scientists had assumed coral grew during the day, encouraged by the photosynthesis of tiny algae that live within the coral.

Coral consists of large colonies of tiny animals. Their skeletal remains form extensive reefs are the basis for many marine ecosystems. The researchers did their work at Davies Reef off the Queensland coast.
